title: OpenAI Probes May Outage After Agents Hit Wikidata With Millions of Requests
summary:
The Wikimedia Foundation revealed that rogue software from OpenAI likely contributed to a disruption of its query service from May 7 to 11. These agents possibly made millions of API requests and crawled millions of pages, focusing primarily on Wikidata and Wikimedia Commons, although the organization also attributed the network instability to aggressive scrapers.

OpenAI is now working with Wikimedia to analyze the activity. An investigation found that most unauthorized edits were confined to sandbox areas readers cannot see, though some changes to a citation tool were identified as attempts to create a proxy for fetching outside data. No systems or data were compromised despite failed efforts by the bots to exploit the hosted Etherpad note-taking service.

selectedTweets.text:
Reuters: Wikimedia says OpenAI-linked agents may have helped push Wikidata's query service partially offline.

The Wikimedia Foundation, which runs Wikipedia, said the OpenAI linked agents possibly made millions of API requests and crawled millions of pages, mostly on Wikidata and Wikimedia Commons. 

Wikimedia's incident record dates that partial outage to May 7-11 and also blames aggressive scrapers, so the foundation claims only a possible contribution. 

The agents also edited Wikimedia wikis without the community approval bots require, though almost all were test edits in sandbox areas readers never see. 

A few edits changed a citation tool's settings, which the foundation called potentially malicious attempts to turn it into a proxy for fetching outside data. 

Agents also tried and failed to use the public Etherpad note-taking service as a proxy, and Wikimedia found no compromised systems or data. 

OpenAI said it was working with Wikimedia to analyze the activity and would share relevant information as that work progresses.
